conventions.assetRoot: Synthetic fixtures resolve assets against a temporary asset root. Files named here are synthetic PNGs created by each test.
conventions.rejectionMessage: A whole-generation rejection is an ordinary frame_rejected whose message starts with the stable prefix "asset_hold <code>"; tests match that prefix.
conventions.refusal: A per-resource refusal keeps the generation accepted and reports state "refused" with a reason code from refusalReasons.
conventions.omission: sourceRect, base, drawSize and canvas may be omitted; explicit null is rejected. drawSize and canvas must appear together. Optional boolean reread defaults to false.
conventions.integers: An integer field accepts only a JSON integer without fraction or exponent; booleans, strings, fractions and 1.0 are rejected.
conventions.numbers: A number field rejects strings, booleans and nonfinite values. Strict JSON cannot spell NaN or Infinity; an overflowing literal such as 1e400 is rejected whether the parser yields infinity or an error. Such cases appear as rawValue text, never as fixture numbers. An overflowing literal rejects its generation as an ordinary recoverable frame_rejected with resyncRequired and the field's code; it is never an error event.
conventions.validators: Ids use the shared retained-id validator (gpui-renderer retained_protocol.rs validate_id). Asset paths use the shared wire-path validator extracted from the tile asset check (protocol.rs:570-577), then AssetRoot::resolve for root and file facts.
conventions.transactionLimit: A transaction over limits.transaction is rejected whole as an ordinary frame_rejected whose message starts "asset_hold transaction_limit".

negotiation.withoutSubscription: Any asset_hold operation rejects its generation with code capability_missing; frame_ack carries no holds or holdCapacity; no asset_holds event is emitted.
negotiation.eligibleWorker: ready advertises asset_holds only from a renderer that runs an eligible hold worker. A renderer without one answers a hello that requires asset_holds with an ordinary error event before any ready, so ready never lists asset_holds while cold requests would stay pending forever. A hello without asset_holds is unaffected.

base.identity: brightness 1, both flips false, rotation 0 and no bottomFade normalize to the same key as an omitted base

charges.base: the guarded bytes after rotation; zero for an identity base
charges.displayCopy: (ceil(deviceWidth) + 2) * (ceil(deviceHeight) + 2) * 4; one guard device pixel on each side. Source crops retain two source pixels on each side.

limits.leaseCeiling: applies to the transaction's collapsed final desired set; at most 1024 new or changed final requests are processed once each

transaction.appliesTo: every hold transaction: a whole reset from its reset:true chunk to its presenting chunk, and each accepted non-reset generation, whose count the per-frame limit already bounds
transaction.counts: every validated asset_hold put and remove of the transaction, across all staged chunks before the final collapse, including operations later superseded or removed
transaction.serialization: an operation's size is the byte length of its compact UTF-8 JSON after validation. Keys appear in this order: op, kind, id, value. value holds revision, reread (always written), asset, then sourceRect only when present, then base only when it is not the identity. sourceRect holds x, y, width, height. base holds brightness, flipX, flipY, rotation, then bottomFade (line, depth) only when present. Strings escape only quote, backslash and control characters. Number fields use the shortest decimal that round-trips binary64, always with a fraction or exponent; negative zero brightness is written 0.0 Optional drawSize follows base, with width then height as binary64 numbers. Optional canvas follows drawSize, with width then height as integers and viewportFit as a string. Both are part of immutable preparation identity and canonical operation bytes.

examples.meaning: display geometry is counted before metadata admission

transaction.exactness: the threshold cases use only strings, integers and booleans, so both sides compute their sizes exactly
transaction.effect: exceeding either total rejects the whole transaction; the staged buffer and its counts are discarded and the committed holds, their jobs and the visible scene stay as they were; the next reset counts from zero

events.waiting: at most one waiting status per current request, so waiting transitions never exceed maxLeasesPerSession however many attempts a closed reader gate or a slow receiver holds back
events.acknowledgements: a frame_ack lists what its generation changed, unchanged by coalescing; its statuses carry the same message bound

canvas.meaning: Logical incoming surface supplied before any frame. It is independent of the currently retained outgoing canvas.

imageBudget.policy: Renderer-configured single complete image ledger; a production numeric ceiling is pending complete measured high-water. Synthetic example limits here are explicit test parameters, not production defaults.
imageBudget.scope: Held, foreground, staging and evictable-cache allocations including scratch/decoder/conversion buffers; one representation is charged once at its strongest owner.
imageBudget.admission: Reclaim evictable cache before refusing new allocations. Never evict held or foreground images to admit a lease. Staging is charged inside the same total and also has a sublimit.
imageBudget.observation: Usage may exceed a newly lowered limit. A truthful over-limit snapshot remains valid; new allocations are refused until admission fits.

holds.message: region of 35615424 bytes exceeds the 33554432-byte hold ceiling

rules: holds lists only requests whose state the generation changed; holdCapacity accompanies holds
the presenting ack of a reset transaction lists every current request
staged acks (presented false) carry holds for the generation that committed them
a held key shared by several leases is counted once in holdCapacity and reported under each id
frame_rejected carries no hold fields and changes nothing

un-emitted transitions coalesce per lease id: an event carries at most one status per id, the newest, so a superseded attempt such as ended changed may never be emitted; the statuses of one event are in the order of each id's newest transition
a waiting status of a request that has since been removed or superseded is never emitted
an event carries at most limits.events.maxStatusesPerEvent statuses, and each message at most limits.events.maxStatusMessageBytes bytes
the Engine discards a status whose (id, revision) it no longer desires or whose attempt is older than one already seen, and accepts a newer attempt without the skipped ones
no event is emitted after shutdown, EOF, fatal or a closed receiver

displayCopies.withoutGeometry: Omitting drawSize and canvas retains the full-size master crop meaning, including nine-slice/plain UI.
displayCopies.source: Each request identifies one source crop; two draw sizes are two preparations. No fixed atlas grid or project scale is inferred.
displayCopies.target: ceil(drawSize * deviceScale) per axis, where deviceScale is the renderer-owned current viewport fit for the declared canvas times backing scale. If either result is at least that master crop axis, hold the original-resolution crop instead. The GPU draws at the declared logical extent. No enlarged bitmap is allocated.
displayCopies.readiness: held only when the current device-scale display copy exists; master residency alone is insufficient.
displayCopies.resize: A changed window or backing scale supersedes the derived preparation and queues its current-scale copy; held is reported once ready.
displayCopies.budget: All copies and decoded/master/foreground/GPU consumers remain under the existing shared renderer budget;1024metadata slots grant no extra memory.
displayCopies.entry: Engine waits without deadline before the first incoming battle composition; real refusal follows the existing renderer-session error path, with no foreground fallback or new retry/cancel UI.
displayCopies.masters: Decoded masters are staging only, one sheet at a time under the same unified budget. They are released once their cell copies exist.

capacity.integerRule: JSON integers only; nonnegative usage, positive limits, within signed64bit range. Checked sums must not overflow.
capacity.sumRule: bytes and count exactly equal their four-owner sums. Per-lease regionBytes/baseBytes are not summed as global usage because representations can be shared.
capacity.subLimit: staging.limitBytes is a sublimit, never added to current allocation bytes.
capacity.overLimit: Truthful usage above current limits is valid; it does not authorize a new allocation.

valid.name: truthful observed usage after limits shrink

invalid.name: invalid owner bytes fractional JSON type
